name: What are drywall finish levels, and which one do I need?

mainEntity.name: What are drywall finish levels, and which one do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall finishes range from basic utility taping to glass-smooth surfaces. Level 1 and Level 2 are typical for hidden utility spaces or under tile substrates where aesthetics do not matter. Level 3 and Level 4 represent common residential standards, suitable for heavy wallcoverings or standard orange peel and knockdown textures. A Level 5 finish involves a full skim coat across the entire wall surface, creating an ultra-flat plane necessary for areas with harsh, direct lighting or high-gloss paint that would otherwise highlight tape seams.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drywall finish levels range from 0 to 5. Level 4 suits standard textured walls, while Level 5 provides a completely smooth skim coat for high-sheen paint.
